m.c: Go with courage, for the one who called you is faithful and walks with you at every step. May his peace guard your heart and his grace sustain you in whatever you face today. Take heart: you do not go out alone, the Lord goes before you.
h: The Gospel of Matthew tells us that Jesus, passing from one place to another, saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax office. He was a tax collector, a profession people of that time looked upon with contempt, since many associated it with foreign rule and unjust levies. Matthew was surely used to being avoided.

But Jesus stopped, looked at him and said only two words: “Follow me.” He did not give him a long speech or first ask him to change his life. And the account adds something striking in its simplicity: “And he rose and followed him.” Matthew left his seat and responded to the invitation of the one who had looked at him in a different way.

Soon after, Jesus was at table in the house, and many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples. The Pharisees, seeing this, asked the disciples why their Teacher ate with that sort of people. Jesus heard them and answered: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.” And he added: “I desire mercy, not sacrifice. For I came not to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”

In time, this tax collector became one of the twelve apostles and the one who left us in writing the first Gospel of the New Testament. His story reminds us that no one is too far away to be reached by the voice of Christ. Where others saw a lost man, Jesus saw a disciple, a witness and a writer of his Word. His life teaches us that God's grace comes first, and that transformation arrives in response to his love. Today, that same invitation remains open for anyone who wants to listen with humility.
m: There are mornings when we feel that our past weighs more than our future. Perhaps we remember mistakes, words we would like to erase or labels others stuck on us long ago. The story of Matthew tells us that Jesus does not stop at our labels. He stops at us, looks at us with love and extends a simple invitation: follow me.

Notice what the psalmist says: “Make me to know your ways, O LORD; teach me your paths. Lead me in your truth and teach me.” Following Jesus is not a leap into the void; it is letting yourself be taught and guided. You do not need to have all the answers to begin the day; it is enough to have a heart willing to learn and to obey step by step.

Now put this into practice. First, before looking at your phone or entering the rush, spend a minute telling the Lord: “Here I am, guide me today.” Second, think of a person you may have looked at from a distance, someone the world often leaves aside, and find a way to greet them with respect or share a kind conversation. Jesus sat at table with those whom others rejected, and we can imitate that gesture.

Finally, remember that Jesus said he desires mercy. If someone disappoints you today, respond with patience; if it is you who fails, return to him without fear, for he is the physician who heals. Rise like Matthew, leave behind what holds you to what was and walk with hope. This day is a new invitation, and the voice calling you is the same one that transformed a tax collector into a witness of the Gospel.
o: Heavenly Father, I thank You for this new day You give me. As I open my eyes, I want to acknowledge that everything I have comes from Your hand: the air I breathe, the light coming through my window and the chance to begin again. Thank You, because Your mercies are new every morning and because Your faithfulness never ceases.

Lord Jesus, just as You called Matthew while he sat at his place of work, today You call me with the same tenderness. You do not look at me for what I have been or for my mistakes, but for what Your grace can do in my life. Help me hear Your voice amid the noise of the rush, and give me a heart willing to rise and follow You without delay.

Teach me Your ways today, guide me in Your truth and do not let me stray from You. Give me eyes to see those who need a friendly hand, and a compassionate heart like Yours so that I despise no one. May my words be kind, may my decisions honor You, and may I be able to say at the end of the day that I walked at Your side. I place this day in Your hands, trusting that You go before me. In Jesus' name, amen.
m.t: A Voice That Says: Follow Me

t.c: Rest now, beloved child, for the Shepherd who cared for you during the day does not fall asleep and does not go away. Let go of your burdens into his hands and close your eyes in peace. May his goodness accompany you tonight and may it wake you tomorrow with a serene heart.
h: Before he was king, David was a shepherd. The Scriptures tell us he tended his father Jesse's sheep in the fields of Bethlehem, and that in that simple and sometimes lonely life he learned what it means to care for the weak. When, years later, he wrote Psalm 23, he was not speaking of theories: he was speaking of what he had lived alongside the flock.

A shepherd leads his sheep to green pastures and guides them beside still waters. He knows that a tired or frightened sheep cannot move forward, and that is why he makes it rest. David looked at this task and understood that God was doing the same with him: “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.” He does not say there would be no dark valleys, but that he would not be alone in them.

He himself acknowledges that he walked through “the valley of the shadow of death.” In the biblical account we see that David faced threats, persecution and nights of anguish. Yet he wrote: “I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.” The rod and the staff were the tools with which the shepherd defended and corrected his sheep, a sign that someone was watching over them.

In another psalm, written in a moment of great danger, David says: “But you, O LORD, are a shield about me, my glory, and the lifter of my head. I cried aloud to the LORD, and he answered me from his holy hill. I lay down and slept; I woke again, for the LORD sustained me.” This shepherd-king learned to sleep in peace, not because there were no problems, but because God watched over his rest. So every time we read this psalm, we listen to the voice of a man who knew God's care up close and wanted to share it with all of us. That trust remains an open invitation for our nights.
m: At the end of the day, it is common for the mind to keep spinning. We replay what we said, what we did not have time to do and what could go wrong tomorrow. But Psalm 23 teaches us a different path: to acknowledge that it is not we who hold up the world, but that a Shepherd cares for us with attention and tenderness.

David wrote that the Lord made him lie down in green pastures and led him beside still waters. Notice the verb: he makes him lie down. Sometimes our weariness is not resolved by one more effort, but by accepting that we can stop. Today you can give yourself permission to stop, because the Lord is in charge.

Here are three practical steps for tonight. First, write on a sheet of paper three things you are grateful for from this day, even small ones. Second, write down what worries you and, paper in hand, give it to God in a low voice, saying: “Lord, this is yours.” Third, turn off the screens a little while before sleeping and slowly read Psalm 23 or repeat the verse: “I lay down and slept.”

The psalmist ends by saying that goodness and mercy will follow him all the days of his life. This means that tomorrow you do not start from zero or alone; God's goodness is already coming behind you, covering your steps. Rest with this certainty. The same Shepherd who has brought you this far will lead you tomorrow to new pastures and give you strength for the road.
o: Lord my God, at nightfall I come before You with a grateful heart. Thank You for sustaining me throughout this whole day, in what went well and also in what I did not understand. You were with me when I got up, when I worked, when I grew tired and when I needed a word of encouragement. I acknowledge that I lacked nothing, because You are my shepherd.

I now give You the concerns I carried today. The difficult conversations, the unsettled matters, the fears that arose in silence and the things left hanging. I do not want to take them to bed like a heavy backpack. I lay them at Your feet, for You are a shield around me, my glory and the lifter of my head.

Forgive me if, today, I acted in haste, with impatience or without remembering You. Cleanse me by Your grace and renew my spirit. Bless my family, my friends and those going through times of pain tonight. Give me quiet sleep, like that of one who trusts in his shepherd, and wake me tomorrow with renewed hope. I lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone make me dwell in safety. Thank You, Lord, for Your faithfulness. In Jesus' name, amen.
